newsitem.title: USA: Britain, Canada to extend bilateral cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Britain, Canada to extend bilateral cooperation.

text.p: Britain and Canada on Friday set a joint agreement to review their relationship in a bid to strengthen ties.
The declaration followed a meeting between Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien and Britain's new Prime Minister Tony Blair before the summit of the Group of Seven industrialized nations and Russia.

"It was agreed that, over the coming months, our two countries would develop a joint programme of work to accentuate further the close dialogue existing between the two heads of government," the joint declaration said.
The two leaders would deepen their relationships at meetings on the fringes of a series of international summit meetings over the next year, it added.
"The process will provide a strong impetus that will bring the relationship into the 21st century and define a new and dynamic footing for the years beyond," the statement said.

The 10-point work programme would include increased contact at ministerial level and joint projects in foreign policy and trade issues. Parliamentary contacts would be reinvigorated and educational links between the two nations encouraged.
New efforts would also be undertaken to encourage science and technology partnerships between firms, the agreement said.
